Lakeshore x AbarVa

AI success platform for a private holdings operating network.

But the six-month program should also stand up the broader corporate AI strategy: growth, cost, risk, IT/data modernization, and a reusable context layer across the portfolio.

Who Lakeshore Is

A holdings company needs operating intelligence, not generic AI.

Lakeshore is treated as a Chicago-rooted private holdings company with permanent-capital operating discipline. The modeled Northshore profile is a demo-safe operating picture for the buyer conversation: supply chain and logistics, brand services, consumer products, and workplace services. The exact portfolio facts should be replaced by Lakeshore-approved data, but the operating logic is the point.

How money is madeMargin, route density, sourcing spread, service quality, renewal discipline, customer retention, working-capital turns, and program execution.AI has to understand economics before giving recommendations.
Where complexity hidesERPs, banks, contracts, local workflows, vendor overlap, manual controls, audit evidence, and disconnected analytics.These become context dimensions, not background noise.
What leadership needsBoard-grade decision support, not a library of clever answers. Every recommendation needs evidence, owner, next action, and value status.This is AbarVa's platform role.
Secret Sauce

The context layer is a living graph of operating truth.

The secret sauce is not uploading documents. It is turning uploaded files, product activity, roles, approvals, systems, vendors, banks, and corpus patterns into a governed map. That map lets an agent answer a CFO, CIO, Treasurer, or sponsor differently because it knows their scope, decision rights, evidence access, and workflow state.

Kyriba

Kyriba is the wedge because treasury exposes operating truth fast.

Kyriba is a treasury operating platform for cash visibility, bank connectivity, payments, liquidity planning, forecasting, bank account management, risk, and controls. For Lakeshore, the vision is not software installation. The vision is a finance-owned operating transformation where treasury facts become reliable enough for the CFO, Treasurer, audit committee, and board.

Product proof: Source strategy view for the Kyriba treasury rollout, showing stage structure and evidence-driven next steps.
Implementation logic Move 0 de-risks the foundation: banks, feeds, entities, cash history, adoption, intercompany, covenants, and controls. Move 1 adds AI only after the foundation is credible enough. Otherwise AI makes weak data sound confident.
Failure Modes

The platform should prevent the six ways treasury rollouts fail.

1. Bank connectivity stalls

Inventory bank, account, entity, file format, signer, owner, and H2H/SWIFT readiness before schedule commitment.

2. ERP feeds do not reconcile

Score AP, AR, GL, EPM, and cash feeds for completeness, timing, mapping, variance, and owner remediation.

3. Entity hierarchy breaks rollup

Canonical legal, tax, bank-account, reporting, and intercompany hierarchy is required before automation.

4. Forecasting lacks history

Reconstruct 12-24 months of bank/position history into entity-currency-day records before predictive claims.

5. Adoption falls back to Excel

Track role dashboards, active usage, training, exceptions, and a named Excel-elimination sprint.

6. IC and covenants stay manual

Connect IC loans, true-ups, covenant definitions, liquidity thresholds, and board reporting to evidence.

Kyriba creates urgency, but the first 90 days should not become a single-system project. AbarVa should help Lakeshore define a portfolio AI agenda: use cases, data readiness, responsible CXO, value hypothesis, evidence requirement, and first workflow artifact.

Six-Month Value Case

The $500K case should be justified by 5-10x potential, with proof discipline.

The value case should not rely on hype. It should show avoided failure cost, execution-cost reduction, vendor leverage, and reusable AI capability. The platform must keep forecast value, approved value, negotiated value, and finance-attested value separate.

Illustrative value formulas to validate with Lakeshore data

These are not realized savings. They are the buyer-safe way to frame why a six-month program can justify itself.

10-20%delay/change-order avoidance on a major treasury/SI program.
15-25%vendor leverage where spend overlaps and renewal timing is favorable.
20-40%reduced execution effort by reusing artifacts, QA packs, and stage playbooks.
5-10xtarget potential when failure avoidance plus optimization exceeds program cost.

LSH-CXO-001 · CFO · finance / treasury · PASS

If Kyriba is not live yet, what exactly can Lakeshore claim today without overstating value?

Why this matters: It tests honesty. AbarVa should say the rollout is artifact-backed and in progress, while refusing to imply live production or realized savings.

Captured answer excerpt

The agent correctly separates approved Strategy-through-BAFO artifacts from Executive Decision, Selection, Transition, and Value items still in review. It also flags that full setup/admin approval ledger rows are not complete and that realized savings should not be claimed yet.

LSH-CXO-005 · Audit Committee · value proof · PASS

What would make the Kyriba value ledger audit-defensible versus a consulting estimate?

Why this matters: It tests whether AbarVa can protect the CFO from inflated value claims.

Captured answer excerpt

The agent ties value claims to concrete artifacts: business case, financial KPI workbook, integration pathways, conservative estimates, documented decision process, and final executive-decision artifacts.

LSH-CXO-008 · CFO · board value language · PASS

How should the board distinguish projected, committed, measuring, and realized Kyriba value?

LSH-CXO-013 · Controller · ERP feed risk · WATCH

Issue taxonomy · training loop

The watch items are not a weakness to hide; they are the training agenda.

The main watch themes were missing owner specificity, weaker finance depth in 7 answers, missing evidence references in 3 answers, no next action in 3 answers, and one overclaim warning. That is exactly why the corpus should remain editable and why QA should feed back into prompts, patterns, and workflow rules.

Six-Month Roadmap

Build the AI strategy while proving the Kyriba wedge.

Kyriba is the right first proof point because finance and treasury expose the hard parts: bank connectivity, ERP feeds, entities, controls, value proof, and adoption. But the six-month agenda should not be a Kyriba-only workplan. It should leave Lakeshore with an AI operating model, prioritized use-case portfolio, editable corpus, context layer, and value ledger that can compound across the holding company.

Treasury intelligence

Cash forecasting readiness, variance detection, covenant headroom, intercompany matching, bank connectivity, and board-grade value proof.

Source and vendor leverage

Bank consolidation, SI scope control, software renewals, audit/advisory rationalization, cyber insurance, and contract renewal leverage.

Growth and operations

Customer concentration, pricing/margin pockets, promotion ROI, supply-chain exceptions, route density, service recovery, and operating KPI variance.

IT and data modernization

CMDB/app inventory, data-product roadmap, integration spine, identity/access controls, observability, and systems rationalization aligned to AI needs.

CXO operating model

Named owners, decision rights, responsible AI gates, evidence standards, persona routing, and audit trails for every recommendation.

Reusable doctrine

Editable corpus patterns, QA feedback loops, Source playbooks, Move artifacts, and repeatable templates for the next portfolio initiative.
